```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                     warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(Shennong)
```

## Scope and source verification

The API provides **23 structural styles** across matrices, distributions,
effect estimates, set intersections and networks, alongside three reusable
atlas themes. Structural styles change panel geometry: triangles, rings,
annotation tracks, paired trajectories, split densities, forests, UpSet,
clone trees and weighted chord ribbons. Typography remains 8 pt. They do not reproduce the papers' biological
results or guarantee identical colors, coordinates, clustering or panel layout.
`style = "classic"` retains each function's original defaults. Explicit palettes
and existing embedding (`nebula`, `glass`) and Sankey (`A`, `B`, `C`) styles remain
available.

The six papers below are the source set. Main figures were inspected for NK,
B, myeloid, fibroblast and CM. For the Science T-cell paper, figure-caption
descriptions were accessible, but the figure images were not independently
inspected; its entries are provisional layout classifications. Supplementary
and extended-data figures are **not an exhaustive part of this inventory**.
The fibroblast paper is a cross-tissue atlas with cancer analyses. The Nature
paper defines *cellular modules*, which are different from gene modules.

```{r papers, results='asis'}
papers <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "zhang-atlas-papers.csv",
                              package = "Shennong"))
papers$Article <- sprintf("[%s (%s), %s](https://doi.org/%s)",
  papers$authors, papers$year, papers$journal, papers$doi)
knitr::kable(papers[c("paper", "title", "Article", "verification")])
```

## Choose a geometry before choosing a style

| Visual family | Representative panels | Input meaning and Shennong route |
|---|---|---|
| Embedding and feature maps | NK 1C–D, 3C–D; B 5D–G | `sn_plot_dim()`, `sn_plot_feature()` preserve supplied embedding coordinates; no velocity or new embedding is inferred. |
| Marker dots | Myeloid 1E; NK 3E; B 5F; fibroblast 3A | `sn_plot_dot(style = "atlas_outline")`: color is expression, size is percent expressing. Named feature lists form marker blocks. |
| Independent bubble encodings | Fibroblast 1F; NK 6B–C; T 2A | `sn_plot_matrix(type = "bubble", size = ...)`: supply Ro/e, interaction potential or effect as color, and frequency, significance or effect as area. Legend titles must name the actual quantities. |
| Expression heatmaps | NK 3A–B; B 5I; myeloid 3B | `sn_plot_heatmap()` keeps the chosen cell/average mode and assay/layer. Paper styles use the ggplot renderer. |
| Quantitative matrices | B 4A; CM 2c, 5f; fibroblast 5A | `sn_plot_matrix()` preserves supplied Ro/e, correlation, activity or model coefficients, including NA. Optional blocks and clustering are explicit. |
| Summary bars | T 1D–E | `sn_plot_barplot(stat = "summary", errorbar = "sd", style = "atlas")` preserves sample means and SD; select SD versus SE explicitly. |
| Sample composition | NK 2B–D; myeloid 3E; B 2A | `sn_plot_sample_boxplot()` and `sn_plot_sample_bar()` retain sample denominators. Samples, not cells, are biological replicates. |
| Distributions | NK 3G; B 5H; CM 4e | `sn_plot_distribution()`, `sn_plot_violin()`: distinguish cell-level distributions from sample-aggregated values with `sample_by`. |
| Correlations and fitted trends | NK 6I; B 2B; myeloid 7E | `sn_plot_association()` retains the chosen correlation and fit. Style does not change test units or P values. |
| Differential expression and enrichment | NK 4; fibroblast 2E–G, 4A–B | `sn_plot_de()`, `sn_plot_enrichment()` style existing statistics; significance thresholds remain analysis choices. |
| Survival and effect intervals | NK 5D–E; fibroblast 4G–H; T 5B | `sn_plot_survival()` renders an existing survival result. A linear coefficient forest (T 4B) must not be interpreted as a Cox HR forest. |
| Communication and module networks | NK 6; CM 2b, 5i; fibroblast 3I | `sn_plot_communication()` styles its native score; `sn_plot_network()` renders supplied edges and nodes. The latter also accepts fixed coordinates for matched network comparisons. |
| Spatial coordinates and features | Fibroblast 5D–F; CM 3, 4g | `sn_plot_spatial*()` uses existing coordinates/sections. Histology and segmented-cell outlines require their original image assets. |
| Set, tree and circular layouts | B 2C/3D/4L; CM 4c; fibroblast 6B | `sn_plot_overlap(style="upset")`, `sn_plot_network(style="clone_tree"/"chord")`, `sn_plot_matrix(style="split_triangle"/"circular")`. Supply sets, topology and scores explicitly. |

Circular phylogenetic dendrograms, Venn diagrams, FACS gates, ATAC tracks,
microscopy and hand-drawn cluster outlines remain outside these structural
styles. Clone trees use supplied rooted topology; they do not reconstruct BCR
lineages. The `raincloud` layout is an adaptation of violin/box/sample-dot
conventions, not a claim of an identical source panel.

## Structural styles and panel references

```{r structural-catalog, results='asis'}
layouts <- sn_list_plot_styles()
layouts <- layouts[layouts$kind == "structure" & !duplicated(layouts$style), ]
knitr::kable(layouts[c("function_name", "style", "reference", "data_requirements")])
```

Use `sn_list_plot_styles("sn_plot_distribution")` to discover styles accepted
by one function. These styles are function-specific: `style="upset"` belongs
to `sn_plot_overlap()`, not to an embedding renderer. The original
`sn_plot_heatmap(mode="average")` accepts matrix structures and forwards
annotation/summary arguments through `...`; `sn_plot_violin()` also accepts
`violin_box`, `raincloud`, `split_violin`, and `stacked_violin`. Use
`sn_plot_distribution()` for tables, explicit assay/layer choices and sample
aggregation. Existing defaults remain unchanged.

The examples below are synthetic layout demonstrations. They are not the
paper's cancer data. The separate Nature workbook recipe uses original values.

```{r matrix-structures, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
set.seed(102)
m <- matrix(rnorm(24), 4, dimnames = list(paste0("State ", 1:4), paste0("Site ", 1:6)))
correlation <- cor(t(m))
p1 <- sn_plot_matrix(correlation, style = "split_triangle",
  compare = correlation * 0.6, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1))
p2 <- sn_plot_matrix(m, style = "circular", midpoint = 0)
patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2)
```

`split_triangle` keeps `x` above and `compare` below the omitted diagonal.
Both axes must have identical ordered IDs. Independent clustering is rejected.
`dendrogram` clusters both axes using Euclidean distance and complete linkage;
its new dendrogram is not claimed to match an unpublished paper tree.

```{r annotated-structure, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
annotation <- data.frame(system = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3), row.names = colnames(m))
sn_plot_matrix(m, style = "annotated", column_annotation = annotation, midpoint = 0)
```

For `heatmap_bar`, supply `row_summary = setNames(values, rownames(m))`;
for `heatmap_density`, supply `column_summary = setNames(values, colnames(m))`.
These tracks display your supplied statistic. `grouped_bubble` requires an
independent non-negative `size` matrix plus a named `row_split` or
`column_split`; area zero remains invisible.

```{r distribution-structures, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
samples <- data.frame(subject = rep(paste0("P", 1:12), 2),
  condition = rep(c("Pre", "Post"), each = 12),
  score = c(rnorm(12), rnorm(12, 1)))
a <- sn_plot_distribution(samples, "score", "condition", style = "raincloud")
b <- sn_plot_distribution(samples, "score", "condition", style = "paired_box", pair_by = "subject")
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)
```

Paired plots require one observation per subject/group/feature and complete
pairs across groups. For cell-level tables, aggregate using a unique specimen
`sample_by` column and identify matched patients with `pair_by`. The plot does
not pair by row order, impute missing subjects or calculate a P value.
`split_violin` draws two horizontal half densities per feature, each normalized
to its own maximum width, with median marks; width is not relative cell count.

```{r effect-and-sets, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
effects <- data.frame(label = c("NK", "B", "Myeloid"),
  estimate = c(-0.5, 0.2, 0.8), lower = c(-0.8, -0.1, 0.4), upper = c(-0.2, 0.5, 1.2))
a <- sn_plot_effect(effects, style = "forest", value_label = "Coefficient (95% CI)")
b <- sn_plot_overlap(list(B = c("S1", "S2", "S3"), T = c("S2", "S4"), Myeloid = c("S2", "S3")))
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)
```

For HR/OR forests use `scale="ratio"` and strictly positive supplied intervals;
the reference becomes one and the axis logarithmic. `identity` uses zero.
UpSet bars count **exclusive** intersections; every ID belongs to exactly one
bar. Empty intersections are omitted; duplicate IDs within a set are rejected.

```{r network-structures, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
links <- data.frame(source = c("A", "A", "B"), target = c("B", "C", "D"), weight = c(1, 3, 2))
a <- sn_plot_network(links, style = "clone_tree")
b <- sn_plot_network(links, style = "chord", weight_label = "Supplied interaction weight")
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)
```

`clone_tree` requires a connected rooted tree; its default branch distance is
unit edge depth, or the supplied `branch_length` column. `chord` requires
non-negative weights; ribbon endpoints and sector widths encode incident
weight, not node counts. `bipartite` uses two explicit node groups.
`rewiring` accepts `compare_edges`; both panels share node coordinates and edge
scales, retaining absent edges as absent. None infer biological interactions.

The repository's `scripts/smoke/atlas-figure-layouts.R` exports all 23 styles to
PDF/PNG and source-data bundles, with an independent 408-value Nature readback.

## Compare the reusable styles

```{r styles}
sn_list_plot_styles()
```

`atlas` uses solid marks and clean atlas panels; `atlas_outline` uses thin
outlined bubbles and open boxplots; `atlas_module` uses sequential purple
activity maps and grey network edges. These are shared presets, not claims
that every panel in one paper has the same palette. Signed matrices can use
`midpoint = 0`; Ro/e matrices can use `midpoint = 1`. Supply `limits` explicitly
when comparing panels on a common scale. No automatic log transform or
significance conversion occurs.

The following is the real 80-cell `pbmc_small` teaching dataset distributed
with SeuratObject, with its original identities and t-SNE. It is not data from
the six cancer papers and is not a validation of their cell labels.

```{r embedding}
pbmc <- SeuratObject::pbmc_small
sn_plot_dim(pbmc, reduction = "tsne", style = "atlas", raster = FALSE)
```

```{r dot-comparison, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
markers <- list(B = c("MS4A1", "CD79A"), T = c("CD3D", "CD2"))
plots <- lapply(c("classic", "atlas", "atlas_outline"), function(style) {
  sn_plot_dot(pbmc, features = markers, style = style) + ggplot2::ggtitle(style)
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1)
```

```{r average-heatmap}
sn_plot_heatmap(pbmc, unlist(markers), layer = "data", mode = "average",
                style = "atlas_outline")
```

Atlas dot styles currently reject `split_by`: Seurat's split-dot color encoding
differs from a shared quantitative scale. Use named feature blocks or separate
panels with explicitly matched limits. Heatmap atlas styles currently require
`backend = "ggplot2"`; the other heatmap renderers retain their native controls.

## Reproduce Nature Fig. 2c from its source numbers

The publisher provides a [source workbook for Fig. 2](https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-025-09053-4/MediaObjects/41586_2025_9053_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx).
Sheet `Fig. 2c`, after its first explanatory row, contains 12 CMs and 34 tissue
columns. Some very small numbers are stored as scientific-notation text;
`as.numeric()` parses them without adding pseudocounts. The recipe below preserves all 408 values and their source order.
Color is capped at 3 for display while source values remain intact.
The paper's dendrogram and exact color lookup are not reconstructed; this
is a new rendering of the supplied numerical matrix, not a modified copy of
the original figure. The original figures are not bundled with Shennong.

```{r cm-recipe, eval=FALSE}
d <- readxl::read_excel("41586_2025_9053_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx",
                         sheet = "Fig. 2c", skip = 1)
roe <- vapply(d[-1], as.numeric, numeric(nrow(d)))
rownames(roe) <- d[[1]]
p <- sn_plot_matrix(roe, style = "atlas_module",
                     palette = c("#FFFFFF", "#FCAE91", "#CB181D"), limits = c(0, 3),
                     value_label = "Ro/e", title = "CM tissue prevalence")
stopifnot(identical(attr(p, "shennong_figure_data")$matrix, roe))
sn_export_figure_bundle(p, "cm-fig2c", width = 240, height = 115)
```

Read-only numeric source matrices are retained in the plot's
`shennong_figure_data` attribute. Figure bundles write them as CSV with an
explicit `.shennong_row` column (or a collision-free variant), together with
the PDF/PNG, figure specification and checksummed manifest. Network bundles
include separate original edge/node tables and rendered coordinates.

The repository script `scripts/smoke/atlas-figure-styles.R` downloads this
workbook only when invoked with `--download`, records its URL and SHA-256,
exports the figure, reads the CSV back and verifies every value. It also
produces a PDF/PNG comparison gallery. Running it without `--download` uses
the existing local workbook and fails clearly if it is missing.

## Supplied matrix and network examples

The next examples use explicitly artificial numbers to demonstrate the
interface; they are not reported biological findings.

```{r bubble, fig.width=5, fig.height=3.5}
score <- matrix(c(0.4, 1.2, 1.8, 0.7, 1, NA), 2,
                dimnames = list(c("State A", "State B"), c("Site 1", "Site 2", "Site 3")))
frequency <- score; frequency[] <- c(5, 20, 40, 10, 15, 0)
sn_plot_matrix(score, type = "bubble", size = frequency,
                midpoint = 1, style = "atlas_outline",
                value_label = "Ro/e", size_label = "Frequency (%)",
                title = "Artificial interface example")
```

```{r network, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
edges <- data.frame(source = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
                    target = c("B", "C", "D", "D"),
                    weight = c(0.3, 0.8, 0.4, 0.6))
nodes <- data.frame(node = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "Isolate"),
                    lineage = c("Group 1", "Group 2", "Group 1", "Group 3", "Group 2"))
sn_plot_network(edges, nodes, group_by = "lineage", style = "atlas_module",
                 weight_label = "Supplied score",
                 title = "Artificial topology; no CM inference")
```

## Main-figure inventory

This index classifies 38 main figures. Routes identify useful renderers;
they do not promise every listed subpanel is reproduced by one function.
Existing trajectory/velocity views retain their own presentation controls.
The three CSV catalogs (papers, figures and layouts) are installed under `system.file("extdata", package =
"Shennong")`, so the classifications and verification status remain inspectable.

```{r inventory, results='asis'}
inventory <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "zhang-atlas-figures.csv",
                                package = "Shennong"))
for (paper in papers$paper) {
  cat("\n\n### ", paper, "\n\n", sep = "")
  rows <- inventory[inventory$paper == paper, -1]
  print(knitr::kable(rows))
}
```
